subject: Request: temporary hold on backup pruning for regulatory audit
messages:
From: Anna Fischer <anna.fischer@clearwellhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: temporary hold on backup pruning for regulatory audit

Hi Grace,

We're starting a regulatory readiness audit next Monday and the auditors have asked us to preserve a subset of logs and nightly backups going back 90 days for a sampling exercise. Our security/compliance team narrowed the scope to: authentication logs, admin API request logs, and daily DB snapshots for tenant clearwell-prod between 2025-06-01 and 2025-09-30.

Can Redwood place a temporary hold on the scheduled backup pruning for that scope while we complete the audit? We also need a mapping of any subprocessors that will touch those backups (e.g., S3 replication, archival partners) and an estimate for how quickly you can produce deletion evidence once the hold is released.

Apologies for the short notice — this came up from the regulator. If you need a PO or formal request, legal is copied here.

Thanks,
Anna Fischer
DPO, Clearwell Health
anna.fischer@clearwellhealth.com
+1 415-555-0192
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Anna Fischer <anna.fischer@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hold on backup pruning for regulatory audit

Hi Anna — thanks for the heads up and totally understand the urgency. We can accommodate a temporary hold, but we need to lock down scope and subprocessors quickly so we can avoid material impact to other customers.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- You confirm the exact dataset identifiers (tenant, snapshot naming pattern, log buckets).
- Redwood to provide subprocessor mapping and a proposed hold length.
- Legal (Kimberly) will draft a short DPA addendum for the hold that includes deletion attestation requirements from subprocessors.

We have two operational options: a) flag the objects in-place and suspend the pruning job for the object prefix, or b) export the objects to a short-term quarantine bucket with stricter retention. Option (a) is faster but requires subprocessors to honor immediate non-deletion requests; option (b) gives a stronger separation but will take longer to copy.

Can you confirm which you prefer (in-place hold vs quarantine export)? We'll await the identifiers and will aim to respond with a subprocessor mapping and timeline within 24 business hours.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 11:15:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary hold on backup pruning for regulatory audit

Kimberly / Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Clearwell's ask. Anna requested an immediate hold for auth logs, admin API logs, and daily DB snapshots for clearwell-prod (June–Sept). She hasn't provided exact object prefixes yet.

Operational notes:
- Current pruning cadence: nightly TTL sweep runs each 02:00 UTC and prunes objects where tag:retire_date < today.
- Suspected storage path for snapshots: s3://redwood-backups/clearwell-prod/db-snapshots/YYYYMMDD/*.
- Auth & API logs: split between s3://redwood-logs/clearwell-prod/auth/ and s3://redwood-logs/clearwell-prod/api/.
- Subprocessors that may touch these: CloudStore (long-term cold tier), GlacierLink (archive provider) via CloudStore replication, and our managed replicator service (runs on EC2 in us-east-1).

Attachments: backup_inventory.csv (compiled prefixes and object counts), dpa_addendum_draft.docx (placeholder language — please redline).

Marissa, can you confirm: a) feasibility of an in-place hold (flag TTL exempt for the prefix) vs export quarantine, and b) expected time to provide deletion evidence (object-delete logs or deletion-certificates) from CloudStore/GlacierLink if we ask them for attestations?

Thanks — Grace
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary hold on backup pruning for regulatory audit

Thanks for the details. I reviewed the draft addendum and have the following suggestions:

- Hold term: propose a 75-day temporary hold from the execution date of the addendum, with a requirement that Clearwell provides formal confirmation when the audit sample is complete earlier. 75 days balances audit cycles and operational risk.
- Deletion attestations: add clause requiring Redwood to obtain a deletion attestation from any subprocessor that performs object-level deletion or archival, and to provide signed evidence within 10 business days of hold release. If a subprocessor cannot provide attestation, Redwood must provide a system-level audit trail (object version delete markers, manifest).
- Subprocessor mapping: include a table in the addendum naming CloudStore (object storage & replication), GlacierLink (cold archive via CloudStore), and ManagedReplicator (Redwood-run EC2 replication). Require subprocessors to confirm support for hold/attestation within 48 hours of notification.

Operational risk note: In-place hold is quicker but leaves the objects in customer buckets — if a subprocessor's lifecycle policy runs outside our control, we may need to push for quarantine export. For high-sensitivity regulated customers I'd prefer quarantine export when time permits.

I'll redline dpa_addendum_draft.docx with the above and attach sample language for deletion attestations.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Anna Fischer <anna.fischer@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hold on backup pruning for regulatory audit

Hi Anna — quick update and proposed plan based on our internal review.

Summary plan:
- Scope: auth logs, admin API logs, and daily DB snapshots for tenant clearwell-prod for 2025-06-01 through 2025-09-30 (please confirm exact bucket/prefix strings).
- Hold approach: we'll perform an in-place hold (flag objects as TTL-exempt) immediately to meet the audit start. If any subprocessor lifecycle policy prevents a reliable in-place hold, we'll fallback to quarantine export (we'll confirm within 24h).
- Hold length: proposed 75 days from DPA addendum execution; Clearwell can request early release when audit sampling completes.
- Subprocessors: CloudStore (object storage & replication), GlacierLink (archive partner), ManagedReplicator (Redwood EC2 replication). We'll notify them and require deletion attestations.
- Evidence: upon release, Redwood will provide either signed deletion attestations from subprocessors or system-level audit manifests showing object delete markers and versions; target delivery within 10 business days.

Next steps for you: confirm the exact prefixes/bucket names and whether you prefer quarantine export vs in-place.

We've started drafting the DPA addendum (DocuSign link below) with Kimberly's proposed language. If that works, sign the addendum and we'll execute notifications to subprocessors immediately.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/boards/packet/REDACTED-DPA-ADDENDUM
Inventory (read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/clearwell/audit-inventory-2025

Appreciate the quick coordination — we'll treat this as high priority.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
